relations.note: Quilaztli-Cihuacoatl raises Chimalman's newborn after the mother dies.
Chimalma accompanies the Mexica group carrying Huitzilopochtli from Aztlan.
Mixcoatl lies with Chimalman, fathers her child, and is later called her husband.
Mixcoatl invades her country and shoots four arrows at her.
Chimalman gives birth to Ce Acatl and dies four days later.
Chimalman conceives Quetzalcoatl after swallowing a precious greenstone.
Copil seeks vengeance against his uncle and rallies neighboring peoples.
Huitzilopochtli discovers the plot and commands Copil’s pre-emptive killing.
relations.source: Historia de los mexicanos por sus pinturas

relations.note: Huitzilopochtli is Copil’s maternal uncle.

relations.myth: Casting Copil’s heart from Quetzalcoatl’s stone seat
relations.note: Copil’s heart is cast near a stone associated with Quetzalcoatl’s departure.
Colonial chroniclers merge Huemac and Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl into one celibate holy ruler.
Huemac serves as Quetzalcoatl’s minister before losing the office through deception.

relations.myth: The foundling destined to divide Tollan
relations.note: Huemac is described ambiguously as Tezcatlipoca’s offering, creation, or trace.
Tezcatlipoca’s deceptive female forms sexually compromise Huemac, costing him his priestly office.
Tezcatlipoca stages lethal spectacles, deceptions, and portents that help ruin Huemac’s Tollan.
As Yaotl, he instigates war and sacrifice and separates followers during Huemac’s collapse.
Huemac tries to dispose of his disguised son-in-law in battle, but Tohueyo triumphs.
Tlaloc’s underwater priest restores maize and conveys the demand for Quetzalxotzin’s sacrifice.
Huemac defeats the Tlaloque at ball and demands literal jade and quetzal feathers.
The Tlaloque withhold rain, greenness, and maize after Huemac rejects their agricultural payment.
Tótec’s first wearing of human skin is placed within Huemac’s destructive reign.
Modern pantheon-building calls Malinalxochitl her daughter, but core narratives provide no parentage.

relations.myth: Comparison of Huitzilopochtli’s hostile elder sisters
relations.note: León-Portilla and later retellings equate them through structural analogy, not early testimony.
Huitzilopochtli directs the migrants to depart secretly while Malinalxochitl sleeps.
Malinalxochitl is consistently described as Huitzilopochtli’s elder sister.
relations.source: Durán; Tovar; Crónica mexicana; Crónica Mexicayotl

relations.note: A Tlaxcalan variant substitutes Coatlicue within Topiltzin’s maternal genealogy.
Huitzilopochtli joins the supernatural conspiracy against Topiltzin in Sahagún’s Spanish account.
Mixcoatl is Topiltzin’s father in the Leyenda genealogy.

relations.myth: Topiltzin recovers his murdered father’s remains
relations.note: Topiltzin recovers or honors Mixcoatl’s bones and establishes mortuary observance.
Disguised Titlacauan shows Topiltzin his decayed appearance and administers intoxicating medicine.
Tezcatlipoca acts as the divine antagonist behind Topiltzin’s humiliation and downfall.
After Topiltzin’s cremation, his heart rises and manifests as the Morning-Star lord.
